cards.name: Minus Back
cards.summary: Live Pathfinder effect that keeps only the frontmost object of a group and cuts away every area where the objects behind it overlap it (the effect version of the Pathfinder panel's Minus Back); the result keeps the front object's paint and stays editable in the Appearance panel. On the overlap plate (orange rounded box behind a blue circle, overlapping, no strokes) the circle came out as a blue crescent: the area the box behind it covered is cut away and the box itself is gone.
use_for: knocking a logo shape out of the front panel of a badge without destroying the parts
editable cut-outs: move the back shapes and the hole in the front shape follows
stencil / punched-hole titles where the cutter shapes sit behind the main shape
avoid: a single path: Illustrator alerts that Pathfinder effects belong on groups, layers or type, and in the harvest render check one rectangle came out unchanged (mean pixel difference 0.0); group the shapes first
shapes that do not overlap: nothing is cut and the back objects simply vanish, leaving only the front object; overlap the cutter shapes with the front one
you want the back object kept and the front ones removed: use Subtract (Minus Front) instead
final print / cutter files: Object > Expand Appearance first so the RIP or plotter sees real paths

params.name: Command
params.does: which Pathfinder operation the live effect performs (all 13 Effect > Pathfinder items store the same 'Adobe Pathfinder' effect with the same option values; they differ only in this code and in the DisplayString label)

pairs_with: Object > Group (apply the effect to the group, not to single paths)
Object > Expand Appearance (bake the result into real paths for output)
Window > Pathfinder panel (destructive version of the same operation)
cards.scripting: Select or reference a GroupItem (or layer / type object), then grp.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe Pathfinder"><Dict data="R Mix 0.5 I Command 4 R TrapTintTolerance 0.05 R TrapMaxTint 1.0 R Precision 10.0 R TrapAspect 1.0 R TrapTint 0.4 B ExtractUnpainted 1 B RemovePoints 0 B TrapReverse 0 B ConvertCustom 1 B TrapConvertCustom 0 R TrapThickness 0.25"/></LiveEffect>'); this Dict syntax round-tripped in the harvest with the default values (every sent value read back). DisplayString is left out because its value contains a space (the harvest could not send it either). Menu route with the current dialog values: app.executeMenuCommand("Live Pathfinder Minus Back") on the selection (on a single path Illustrator shows an alert first). Chain-order gotcha (gallery, 2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect appends the Pathfinder effect to the group's art style after its fill/stroke stack, where it acts on the group's own empty paint (blank or unchanged result); the Effect menu puts it at the head of the chain, on the group's contents. The gallery saves the file, moves the effect to the head of the group's chain, reopens and re-renders: that route matched the Effect-menu control pixel for pixel.
cards.non_destructive: yes: live effect stored as 'Adobe Pathfinder' in the Appearance panel; double-click to edit, Object > Expand Appearance to make it permanent
cards.cost: light on a few simple shapes; recomputes the boolean geometry on every edit, so large groups or long type slow redraw

review.changes: single-path avoid line reworded: the 0.0 render means the rectangle was left unchanged, not erased; Command 'does' corrected: the items also differ in DisplayString, not only in Command

verified.note: On the overlap plate only the frontmost blue circle is left, with the part the box behind it overlapped cut away (a blue crescent), in the circle's own paint, as the card describes; the stale vector-plate prediction in avoid was replaced.

cards.name: Outline
cards.summary: Live Pathfinder effect that splits the group's artwork into its component edge segments: every fill becomes an unfilled hairline path in that fill's colour and the original strokes are dropped, so solid shapes read as faint line drawings (the harvest render of a filled, stroked rectangle became a thin outline in the fill colour with the stroke gone, mean pixel difference 19.819). Exact stroke weight of the result was not measured. On the overlap plate (orange rounded box behind a blue circle, overlapping, no strokes) both shapes became faint 1-px hairlines in their fill colours, the box's edge continuing inside the circle, with no fill left.
use_for: wireframe / blueprint look from solid flat artwork while keeping the originals editable
seeing where overlapping shapes cut each other before a Divide or trap job
line-art version of a filled logo for a one-colour engraving mock-up (expand and restroke afterwards)
avoid: you need a controllable outline weight: the resulting lines are thin; expand the appearance and set the stroke yourself, or simply remove the fill and add a stroke
a single path: Illustrator alerts that Pathfinder effects belong on groups, layers or type; group first

stroke-only artwork such as the open, unfilled zigzag on the test plate: it has no fill to outline and its stroke is dropped (ExtractUnpainted also deletes unfilled objects), so expect it to disappear (not verified)
gradient-filled shapes: how the gradient colour carries onto the outline was not checked; verify on the frame

cards.name: Soft Mix
cards.summary: Live Pathfinder effect that divides overlapping shapes into separate faces and fills each overlap with a blend of the colours involved, so the front artwork looks partly see-through like tinted acetate; Mix is the mixing rate (dialog 'Pathfinder Options'; stored 0.5, read as the dialog's 50%, mapping inferred). Like Trim it drops strokes: on a single stroked rectangle the Soft Mix and Trim harvest renders both kept only the fill colour and differed from the plain shape by the same amount (1.849). On the overlap plate (orange rounded box behind a blue circle, overlapping, no strokes) at Mix 0.5 the overlap lens came out a muted violet-blue (105,101,179) and the rest kept its colours.
use_for: flat 'transparent overlap' colour mixes for posters and infographics that print as solid flat-colour faces instead of live transparency
Venn-diagram circles whose overlaps show the mixed colour
screen-print style overlapping ink shapes where each overlap must be its own separable colour
avoid: shapes that do not overlap: nothing mixes and only strokes are dropped; overlap the shapes (the overlap plate's lens is where the mix shows)
true transparency or blend modes are what you want: use the Transparency panel opacity or a blend mode instead, which stays smooth over gradients and images
a single path: Illustrator alerts that Pathfinder effects belong on groups, layers or type; group first
the menu route opens the Pathfinder Options dialog; script it with applyEffect to set Mix without a dialog

cards.name: Trap
cards.summary: Live Pathfinder effect for print prepress: where two differently coloured objects touch it adds a thin overlapping trap shape (lighter colour spread into the darker, or the reverse) so press misregistration cannot open white gaps; it makes nothing where colours do not touch. No render here showed it: on the overlapping plate shapes the PNG export was identical to the plate through the script and the Effect menu, and in a CMYK document colours moved by under 8 levels with no visible trap band, so check traps with Overprint Preview or separations, not a flat export.
use_for: preparing spot-colour packaging or label artwork for offset or flexo when the printer asks for traps
screen-print separations where adjacent inks must overlap slightly
checking where traps would fall, with Overprint Preview on
avoid: screen or web output: traps only matter for separated print and add stray slivers

expecting to see it in a PNG / JPG export or on screen without Overprint Preview: the gallery render of overlapping fills (RGB) was identical to the plate and a CMYK test shifted colours by under 8 levels; and objects that do not touch get no trap at all
gradients, images and very small type: trap a simple flat-colour group, or leave trapping to the printer's RIP / in-RIP trapping
the menu route opens the Pathfinder Options dialog; script it with applyEffect for unattended use
